sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, while Members support the introduction of a Certificate of Medical Need to curb abuse, we must be clear-eyed about who we may have left behind.

sections.label: GPC urges flexible implementation
sections.summary: The GPC urges that implementation be flexible, affordable and clearly communicated so administrative complexities, cost or narrow definitions do not exclude or penalise dependent users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The GPC therefore urges that implementation be flexible, affordable and clearly communicated, so that administrative complexities, cost or narrow definitions do not unintentionally exclude or penalise those who depend on these devices the most.

sections.label: GPC calls for transition period
sections.summary: The GPC calls for a sensible transition period prioritising education and understanding, and discretion where users act in good faith.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: At the same time, the GPC calls for a sensible transition period, one that prioritises education and understanding, and exercises discretion where users are acting in good faith and adjusting to new rules.

sections.label: Speed limiter regime expanded 2024
sections.summary: In 2024, the speed limiter regime was expanded to include lorries with a maximum laden weight between 3,501 and 12,000 kilogrammes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2024, the speed limiter regime was expanded to include lorries with a maximum laden weight of between 3,501 kilogrammes and 12,000 kilogrammes.

sections.label: Speeding accidents involving heavy vehicles fall
sections.summary: Speeding-related accidents involving heavy vehicles decreased by 28% from 25 cases in 2024 to 18 cases in 2025 as more lorries installed speed limiters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The number of speeding-related accidents, including fatal ones, involving heavy vehicles has decreased by 28% from 25 cases in 2024 to 18 cases in 2025, as more lorries installed speed limiters last year.

sections.label: Speed limiter installation assistance for businesses
sections.summary: 94% of lorries due by 1 January 2026 installed speed limiters, with Enterprise Singapore, Traffic Police and industry support measures described.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: On assistance provided to businesses, in this first phase of speed limiter installation, 94% of the lorries that needed to install by 1 January 2026 – or about 2,300 lorries – had completed their installation before the deadline.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To support SMEs, Enterprise Singapore has expanded Productivity Solutions Grant support to cover speed limiters for eligible SMEs that install between 1 October 2025 and 31 March 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Beyond this, the Traffic Police has introduced UN ECE R89 as a third approved speed limiter standard.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Traffic Police has also worked with the industry to significantly increase installation capacity, expanding the number of authorised agents more than six-fold since January 2025, to 70 currently.

sections.label: Outsourcing arrangement and enforcement automation
sections.summary: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the outsourcing arrangement to private sector companies, and the amendments do not involve automation of enforcement decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked for details about the outsourcing arrangement to private sector companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: These amendments do not involve the automation of enforcement decisions.

sections.label: Sentencing guidelines and mobility scooter medical assessment
sections.summary: MHA is working with the Sentencing Advisory Panel to publish sentencing guidelines for dangerous and careless driving, and doctors and occupational therapists will assess medical needs for mobility scooter use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Building on this, MHA is working with the Sentencing Advisory Panel, chaired by Justice Tay Yong Kwang, to publish sentencing guidelines for the offences of dangerous and careless driving.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: At the outset, I wish to make clear that we are not banning the use of mobility scooters but safeguarding them for those who truly need them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Several Members, like Ms Joan Pereira, Ms Choo Pei Ling and Dr Haresh Singaraju spoke about how medical needs will be assessed to allow for the use of mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will need the support of our doctors and occupational therapists (OTs), to assess the medical needs to determine whether a person's medical conditions lead to mobility challenges that require a mobility scooter.

sections.label: Risk-managed exemptions for mobility scooters
sections.summary: Exemptions include seniors aged 70 and above, existing Government-subsidised mobility scooter owners, and those who applied for MOH disability schemes for mobility or transferring needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Risk-managed exemptions include seniors aged 70 and above, those who have already obtained Government-subsidised mobility scooters and those who have applied for MOH disability schemes to help with Activities of Daily Living (ADL) needs in "mobility" and/or "transferring".

sections.label: No subsidies for Certificate of Medical Need visits
sections.summary: Healthcare subsidies will not be given for visits made solely to obtain the Certificate of Medical Need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Healthcare subsidies will not be accorded for visits made solely to obtain the Certificate of Medical Need.

sections.label: Delivery riders without mobility challenges
sections.summary: PMAs are not the right mode of transport for delivery riders without mobility challenges, who can switch to other devices or vehicles before 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: For delivery riders without mobility challenges, PMAs are not the right mode of transport for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: They can continue their trade by switching to other devices or vehicles before 1 June 2026.

sections.label: Lowering PMA speed limit to six kilometres per hour
sections.summary: The speed limit was lowered to six kilometres per hour to peg it to brisk walking speed since PMAs replace walking.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In accepting the recommendation to lower the speed limit to six kilometres per hour, our primary consideration was to peg the speed to brisk walking speed since PMAs are a replacement for walking.

sections.label: Registration deadline for existing mobility scooter users
sections.summary: Stakeholders had time to change to compliant devices before the PMA rules commence on 1 June 2026, but existing mobility scooter users get until 1 January 2029 to register and change to compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Affected stakeholders, including retailers and users, have had time to change to compliant devices before the PMA rules commence on 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: But we will provide more time, until 1 January 2029, for existing mobility scooter users to register their devices and change to devices that comply with the new maximum device speed of six kilometres per hour.

sections.label: Current PAB registration cost
sections.summary: The current cost of registering power-assisted bicycles is $50.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As a comparison, the current cost of registering PABs is $50.

sections.label: Mobility scooter registration framework
sections.summary: Registration and identification marks show the device's unique identification number, not owner details, and only individuals with a Certificate of Medical Need or exempted can generally register mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Registration and identification marks will display the device's unique identification number rather than personal details of the owner, similar to e-scooters, where it is a sticker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In addition, as a general rule, only individuals granted a Certificate of Medical Need or exempted from the requirement can register mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The registration framework will allow families to share a single mobility scooter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Registration is for the mobility scooter to ensure device compliance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: It is not an offence to ride a mobility scooter that is registered to another person as long as the user is granted a Certificate of Medical Need or exempted.

sections.label: Periodic inspections for PMAs
sections.summary: Periodic inspections are required for e-scooters, and mandating them for PMAs to check dimensions and speed limits must be weighed against the burden on users.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Today, periodic inspections are required for e-scooters to check that they remain compliant with the UL2272 standard and have not been illegally modified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The benefits of mandating periodic inspections for PMAs solely to check dimensions and speed limits must be weighed against the burden on users.

sections.label: Online sales of non-compliant devices
sections.summary: LTA works with e-commerce platforms Carousell, Lazada and Shopee to take down listings of non-compliant devices, and will look at strengthening rules for online sales and advertising.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: LTA actively works with major e-commerce platforms like Carousell, Lazada and Shopee to take down listings of non-compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will look at how we can strengthen rules for online sales and advertising in our legislation.

sections.label: ERP payment penalties
sections.summary: Most missed ERP payments are due to genuine oversight rather than intent to avoid payment, so this amendment makes penalties more proportionate to the offence.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Indeed, most missed ERP payments are due to genuine oversight rather than an intent to avoid payment.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: This amendment would therefore make the penalties more proportionate to the offence.

sections.label: Distance-based charging implementation
sections.summary: The speaker does not intend to implement distance-based charging immediately.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: As I mentioned yesterday, I do not intend to implement distance-based charging immediately.

sections.label: OBU exemption for classic vehicles
sections.summary: Vehicles with unresolvable technical problems, such as old cars on Classic or Vintage Vehicle schemes, will be exempted from installing an OBU.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Where technical problems cannot be resolved such as old cars on the Classic or Vintage Vehicle schemes, we will exempt them from the requirement to install an OBU.
